Replace the current input modality with {modality}. Preserve the visual signature.
Reshape the particle distribution from its current form into {form}.

directives.directive: Strip the on-screen UI to a single pulsing 3-char code in the corner. No buttons, no overlays.
Add depth-cued fog and DOF — particles further from camera fade and blur.
Quantize the color output to {n} discrete steps to give a posterized risograph feel.

directives.directive: If audio input is present, make the response 2x more dramatic — add chromatic aberration and shockwave on bass hits.
Reduce the piece to grayscale + one accent color {accent}. Restraint over saturation.

If the parent loads a 3D model and samples its surface as a point cloud (PLYLoader / GLTFLoader + MeshSurfaceSampler), swap the loaded model to {model}. Use the URL exactly as given. If the URL ends in .glb or .gltf, use GLTFLoader and traverse the scene for the first mesh whose geometry has position attribute, then build the sampler from that geometry. Re-normalize the bounding box to fit the existing camera framing. Keep the rest of the piece (palette, gestures, animation) intact. If the parent does NOT use a model loader, instead introduce one: load the model URL and replace the procedural particle distribution with a 60k surface sampling of the loaded mesh.

On a piece that uses a real-object point cloud, change how the cloud disperses on input. New rule: {law}. The rest pose (the recognizable object) should remain when input is neutral; the dispersion is what reads on interaction.

particles spiral around the object's vertical axis as they disperse
the object dissolves into a flock of birds (cohesion + alignment + separation rules)
particles tear along voronoi cell boundaries — the figure shatters
wind from one side of the screen — particles drift in that direction, fall as gravity pulls them
